evidence_basis.source_snapshot: 20261008.1 code before this iteration, plus the saved final proposal

scope.boundary: Approved MS1 frontend prototype: two anonymous readers each select five favorites, then compare five bridge books and per-reader reasons.
scope.state_limit: Current-page interactions only; no new accounts, remote collaboration, persistence, or model-performance promises.

roles.responsibility: Priorities, scope, final interaction decisions, and browser verification
Hierarchy, feedback, touch layout, and restrained motion
Ambiguity, state continuity, keyboard behavior, and accessibility limits

reader_personas.situation: A reader cannot find familiar titles in the sample catalogue.
reader_personas.task: Understand the sample boundary and recover to available books.
reader_personas.hypothesis: Clear sample context and search recovery may help the reader continue.

reader_personas.situation: Partners have different tastes and need to compare reasons and ranking modes.
reader_personas.task: Compare candidates, express interest, and distinguish ranking from a shared choice.
reader_personas.hypothesis: Keeping opinions on retained books may support continuous comparison.

reader_personas.situation: Two readers with limited time take turns on one phone.
reader_personas.task: Complete both sets of five, hand over the phone, and confirm a shared pick.
reader_personas.hypothesis: Visible progress, explicit handoff, and measured shelf spacing may reduce backtracking.

source_observed_friction.observation: The baseline said interest was optional while confirmation required two Interested votes.
source_observed_friction.interpretation: The disabled confirmation button could be hard to understand.
source_observed_friction.decision: Keep the explicit two-Interested guard and clarify that browsing can skip voting, but confirmation requires both readers.

source_observed_friction.observation: The baseline cleared all votes and the shared choice when ranking changed.
source_observed_friction.interpretation: Readers could need to repeat opinions on books still in the shortlist.
source_observed_friction.decision: Retain votes by book ID and keep a valid shared choice. The helper intentionally mutates current state and copies retained vote containers so old nested references are not modified.

source_observed_friction.observation: The baseline candidate-arrow handler did not exclude vote buttons.
source_observed_friction.interpretation: An arrow key could switch books during an interest interaction.
source_observed_friction.decision: Arrow keys on vote buttons must not change candidates; retain explicit Previous/Next controls.

source_observed_friction.observation: The baseline used a fixed 115px body reserve while the bottom shelf could expand to 70dvh.
source_observed_friction.interpretation: Shelf expansion or viewport changes could cover content; this was a layout risk, not an observed user failure.
source_observed_friction.decision: Use ResizeObserver to reserve the shelf's actual height, with additional body padding.

source_observed_friction.observation: The baseline used Both for the mixed genre category and ambiguous balance/average labels; the first recommendation was visually prominent.
source_observed_friction.interpretation: Readers might confuse a category, recommendation order, and a shared decision. These remain hypotheses.
source_observed_friction.proposal: Keep sample boundaries, ranking meaning, and shared-choice status explicit.

root_decisions.confirmation_guard: Confirmation requires both readers to choose Interested. Changing a vote away from Interested invalidates that shared choice.
root_decisions.interest_copy: Browsing does not require voting; explicit shared confirmation does.
root_decisions.ranking_helper: Intentionally mutate current state, retain votes for current book IDs, and copy retained vote containers to protect old nested references.
root_decisions.seed_edits: Seed edits still clear votes and the shared choice.
root_decisions.keyboard: Arrows on vote buttons do not change candidates.
root_decisions.mobile_spacing: ResizeObserver supplies the bottom shelf's measured reserve.

browser_checks.status: Passed as reported by the product lead

results.result: Recovered from a missing-title search to available sample books.
Cancelling preserved an existing one-book selection; explicit sample replacement also worked.
Per-reader reasons and summary labels displayed correctly.
ArrowRight on a vote button left the candidate unchanged.
Expanded evidence stayed open after voting.
The explicit two-Interested confirmation flow passed.
Switching to average ranking retained the same candidate's votes and shared choice.
Removing and re-adding a seed cleared votes and the shared choice.
Manual share text included the current chosen book.
No console errors were observed during these checks.

remaining_checks.checked: ArrowRight on a vote button did not switch candidates. Previous/Next browsing and Escape returned focus to the matching result. Closing manual copy returned focus to the visible Share shortlist disclosure.
remaining_checks.remaining: ArrowLeft on all voting controls and the complete Tab/Enter/Space path were not exhaustively checked.

remaining_checks.check: Map drag, keyboard traversal, and focus visibility after pan or zoom.
Text zoom and an actual software keyboard. Viewport checks do not establish these results.
Verify content and feedback under actual prefers-reduced-motion browser emulation.
Whether readers understand sample boundaries, ranking labels, optional browsing, and shared confirmation. No usability outcome is claimed.

small_copy_proposals.confirmation_help: You can browse without voting. To confirm a shared pick, both readers need to choose Interested.
small_copy_proposals.reader_handoff: Your five are kept. Reader 2, your turn.
small_copy_proposals.ranking_hint: Changing the order keeps your interest in books that stay on the shortlist.
small_copy_proposals.voice_intent: Use concrete, relaxed language about both readers and the shared decision; avoid destiny, emotional measurement, or success-rate claims.

motion_iteration.purpose: Show entry, direction, selection, and confirmation without continuous decoration.
implemented: Cover selection and shelf arrival feedback
browser_checks: Directional classes and computed reading-next/reading-previous animations matched the next and previous book.
Computed card transforms changed during sorting, while retained interests and the shared choice stayed attached to the same book.
